title: friction-diary-and-mini-experiments-collection-2025-08-21
summary: Working notebook that collates frontline friction reports from May–Aug 2025, clusters into 5 micro-themes, and proposes 7 low-effort experiments (probes) for validation. Emphasis on quick wins that reduce token spend friction and improve model fallback clarity for enterprise customers.
body:
Purpose:
- Capture raw friction observations from CS calls, SRE alerts, and account engineering notes (May–Aug 2025).
- Synthesize into compact problem statements and hypotheses.
- Offer low-cost, short-run experiments that product/eng can pick up.

How this doc was compiled:
- Source channels: weekly CS roundup notes, 12 recorded customer calls (redacted), SRE incident timelines, and 24 Slack snippets in #cs-inbox.
- Filtering: included items where customers explicitly asked for changes or where CS recommended a product tweak to avoid recurring support work.

Topline micro-themes (ranked by frequency & operational cost):
1) Unclear fallback behavior during model OOMs or timeouts (high freq, high support cost)
2) Cost surprises from long streaming sessions (medium freq, medium cost)
3) Latency spikes when autoscaling cold GPUs (medium freq, high user-facing impact)
4) Embedding mismatch across model variants (low freq, high product risk for search accuracy)
5) Console opacity: per-route token attribution and billing labels are confusing (high freq, low engineering cost)

Representative customer vignettes (anonymized):
- "We had a customer-facing flow where the chat just cut off — they couldn't tell if it was a transient error or a model limit. We rolled to a smaller model, but the UX isn't obvious and support had to manually explain." — Enterprise security product
- "Streaming kept charging for a long background session; we couldn't reconcile billing with observed usage because our app uses many small streaming fragments." — Mid-market SaaS
- "Cold start latencies kill our demo flows; we sometimes get spikes of 5-8s which ruins the product demo." — AI-native startup

Hypotheses (short):
- H1: Explicit explicit-fallback messaging + telemetry reduces support tickets about cutoffs by >40% in 8 weeks.
- H2: Aggregated streaming-metering (session-level) will make billing disputes drop by 30% when exposed in Console.
- H3: Small pre-warm buffer (soft cushion) for autoscaled GPUs reduces 95th latency by 20% for demo workloads without increasing monthly infra cost >5%.

Proposed mini-experiments (probes) — quick, measurable, low-risk:
1) Fallback Signal + UX shim (owner: Daniel K) — implement a server-side tag in responses when a fallback/variant is used ("x-redwood-fallback: true") and a Console flag to show it in logs for 30 trial customers. Metrics: #support tickets mentioning "fallback" and avg time to resolution. Est. dev effort: 2–3 days.
2) Streaming Session Metering (owner: Aisha P) — create a session id that groups small streams (client-side SDK patch + backend aggregation). Expose session token summary in Console. Metrics: #billing disputes, CS time spent reconciling. Est. dev effort: 1 week.
3) Pre-warm demo lane (owner: SRE lead) — reserve tiny pool of warm instances with short TTL for accounts tagged as demo. Metrics: 95th latency for demos, cost delta. Est. dev effort: infra: 3 days + config.
4) Embedding variant checker (owner: Laura M) — add a comparison page that runs 50 sample queries across two embedding models and reports divergence. Metrics: embedding drift score, customer acceptance. Est. dev effort: 4 days.
5) Token-labeling toggle in Console (owner: Product) — allow toggling "detailed token breakdown" for a route; include summarized reason labels (prompt, system, assistant). Metrics: CS calls about billing clarity. Est. dev effort: 2 days.
6) Canary alert for model OOMs (owner: Platform eng) — raise immediate short-lived alert and synthesize a one-click rollback to last good model. Metrics: #incidents with manual rollback time. Est. dev effort: 3 days.
7) "Quicknote" in support UI (owner: CS tooling) — snippet templates for frontline to paste into incidents highlighting whether fallback was used and if cached prefixes were hit. Metrics: Mean incident triage time. Est. dev effort: 2 days.

Prioritization rationale (fast scoring):
- Score factors: customer impact (3), engineering effort (1 low–3 high), probability of success (1–3).
- Highest combined score: 1) Fallback Signal + UX shim, 2) Streaming Session Metering, 3) Pre-warm demo lane.

Open questions / unknowns to validate quickly:
- Will customers accept the Console changes or do they want API-level flags first? (ask 3 pilot accounts)
- How much does pre-warm buffer cost at scale for >100 demo accounts? (SRE cost sim)
- For embedding checker, which sample set is representative? (product to propose 3 canonical sets)

Quick action plan (next 4 weeks):
- Week 1: Align owners and set success metrics for probes 1–3. Create Jira tickets (JIRA-CS-2981 tentative).
- Week 2: Ship fallback telemetry header + Console log flag behind feature gate for 30 pilot orgs.
- Week 3: Implement session id aggregation in SDK alpha and test on staging; schedule call with 2 mid-market customers for feedback.
- Week 4: Run cost simulation for pre-warm lane; if cost <5% uplift, pilot with 5 demo-tagged orgs.

Metrics dashboard suggestions (minimal):
- Support tickets per week mentioning "cutoff", "fallback", "token billing"
- Average triage time (CS) pre/post probe
- 95th/99th latency for demo-tagged routes
- Billing disputes opened vs. resolved within 7 days

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Adding telemetry headers causes SDK churn. Mitigation: make header optional and behind SDK opt-in.
- Risk: Pre-warm costs escalate. Mitigation: TTL-based automatic drain and conservative pilot pool.

Appendix: quick log snippets (redacted)
- "...response stopped mid-sentence, no error code in logs, customer assumed model crashed" — ticket# 1124
- "billing — we see many small streams for the same session id, billed as separate sessions" — account lead note

Requests to product/eng for triage meeting:
- Product: choose 2 pilot orgs and confirm acceptance criteria for fallback UX (due: 2025-09-10)
- Eng: estimate infra cost for pre-warm lane at 5/50/200 accounts (due: 2025-09-12)
- CS: prepare 3 customer vignettes and secure pilot consent for telemetry testing (due: 2025-09-08)

Notes to self:
- Keep experiments visible in #cs-experiments channel.
- Tag results into Confluence page for playbook creation.

End of notebook.
